module: People's rights: what customers and staff can ask for

lesson.title: Complaints, courts and compensation
lesson.summary: Choose between a complaint, a court action and a compensation claim, and see how liability is shared.

prerequisites.reason: A complaint is lodged with a supervisory authority.
Court action is brought against a controller or processor.

blocks: **Complaint** (Article 77): every data subject may complain to a **supervisory authority**, in particular in the EU country where they live, where they work or where the infringement allegedly took place.
The authority must inform the complainant of the progress and outcome.
**Court** (Article 79): a person may also go to court against a controller or processor. This is **without prejudice** to a complaint: one route does not have to come before the other.
Proceedings may be brought where the controller or processor has an establishment, or where the person habitually resides, unless the defendant is a public authority exercising public powers.
**Representation** (Article 80): a person may mandate a properly constituted not-for-profit organisation, active in data protection, to complain or go to court on their behalf.
EU countries may also allow such bodies to act without a mandate.
**Compensation** (Article 82(1)): **any person** who has suffered **material or non-material damage** from an infringement has a right to compensation from the controller or processor.
Recital 146 says damage should be interpreted broadly, and compensation should be full and effective.

items: A controller involved in the processing is liable for damage caused by infringing processing.
A processor is liable only if it breached its own processor obligations or acted outside or contrary to the controller's lawful instructions.
Either is exempt only if it proves it is **not in any way** responsible.
Where several are responsible, **each is liable for the entire damage**. Whoever pays may claim back the others' shares.

blocks: Suppose Sunfield's payroll firm, breaking its own security duties, leaks salary data. Affected staff could claim against Sunfield and against the firm.
If both are responsible, either can be made to pay the full amount and then recover the other's share.

blocks.text: These Sunfield examples are **illustrations**. A real assessment depends on all the facts.

questions.prompt: A customer living in Austria believes Sunfield, based in Germany, misused her data. Where may she complain?

options.blocks: With the Austrian authority, among other options
options.reason: Article 77(1) names the country of habitual residence.

options.blocks: Only in Germany, where Sunfield is
options.reason: Article 77 offers several countries.

options.blocks: Only at the European Commission
options.reason: Complaints go to a supervisory authority.

variants.prompt: A customer living in Austria wants to complain about a business in Germany. Under Article 77, where may she complain?

options.blocks: Only in Germany, where Sunfield is
options.reason: Article 77 offers several countries.

options.blocks: Only at the European Commission
options.reason: Complaints go to a supervisory authority.

options.blocks: With the Austrian authority, among other options
options.reason: Article 77(1) names the country of habitual residence.

questions.prompt: Must she complain to a regulator before going to court?

options.blocks: Yes, a complaint must always come first
options.reason: Neither route is a precondition for the other.

options.blocks: Only the regulator can go to court
options.reason: Article 79 gives the right to the data subject.

options.blocks: No, court action is available as well
options.reason: Article 79 is without prejudice to Article 77.

variants.prompt: Is a complaint a precondition for a court action under Article 79?

options.blocks: Only the regulator can go to court
options.reason: Article 79 gives the right to the data subject.

options.blocks: No, court action is available as well
options.reason: Article 79 is without prejudice to Article 77.

options.blocks: Yes, a complaint must always come first
options.reason: Neither route is a precondition for the other.

questions.prompt: A customer suffered distress, but no financial loss, from an infringement. Can she claim compensation?

options.blocks: Only if the regulator fines Sunfield first
options.reason: Article 82 has no such condition.

options.blocks: Yes, non-material damage is covered
options.reason: Article 82(1).

options.blocks: No, only financial loss counts
options.reason: Article 82(1) covers non-material damage.

variants.prompt: Does Article 82 cover damage that is not financial?

options.blocks: Yes, non-material damage is covered
options.reason: Article 82(1).

options.reason: Article 82(1) covers non-material damage.

options.reason: Article 82 has no such condition.

questions.prompt: The payroll processor broke its own duties, causing a leak. Who can be liable to the staff?

options.blocks: Each can be liable for the entire damage
options.reason: Article 82(4), with recourse under 82(5).

options.blocks: Only the processor
options.reason: The controller involved may also be liable.

options.blocks: Only Sunfield, because processors are never liable
options.reason: Processors are liable when they breach their own duties.
